# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is a short, fat, and bald man with a fringe of hair around his ears, a round face, and prominent blue eyes. When enraged, his face turns purple and his eyes stick out. He looks quite neat and trimmed after his wife cleans his patched clothes and cuts his hair.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P21](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0021), [v2 c25 P46](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0046)_

## Personality

Mr. Harrison is extremely outspoken, abrupt, and prone to outbursts of temper, though he quickly regains his composure and feels repentant. He values plain truth and does not hesitate to speak his mind, which leads others to view him as a crank. Despite his rough and crabbed exterior, he possesses a good-natured, sociable side, enjoys company, and appreciates quiet humor. He is reluctant to spend money needlessly and holds strong personal views on manners and discipline.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P42](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0042), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c4 P36](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0036), [v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008)_

## History

In April, Mr. Harrison bought Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, moving from New Brunswick. He initially gained a reputation as a eccentric bachelor, keeping irregular meal hours, leaving dishes unwashed, and keeping a swearing parrot named Ginger. He got into a heated dispute with Anne Shirley after her Jersey cow broke into his oatfield, but when Anne accidentally sold his cow and came to apologize, he quickly forgave her and accepted a homemade cake as a peace offering. The two soon developed a warm friendship, frequently visiting each other across the fields. When a lightning strike hit his house and killed Ginger, Anne went over to comfort him in his grief. Shortly afterward, his estranged wife Emily arrived in Avonlea after seeing a newspaper note, and the two reconciled and resumed married life together.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P7](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0007), [v2 c1 P10](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0010), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c2 P35](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0035), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P28](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0028), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c24 P41](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0041), [v2 c24 P43](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0043), [v2 c25 P9](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0009), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P50](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0050), [v2 c25 P60](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0060)_

## Background by volume

- Hails from New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Obtained his parrot Ginger from his brother, a sailor  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>

## Quotes

> I can't help speaking out just what I think and folks must take me as they find me.  <sub>[v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023)</sub>

> I'm a terrible outspoken old fellow, that's all . . . awful apt to tell the truth, no matter if it is a bit plain.  <sub>[v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>

> Mark my words, you'll never manage the young fry unless you keep a rod in pickle for them. The thing is impossible.  <sub>[v2 c4 P38](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0038)</sub>

> I'm a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there's something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it's such a pleasant sensation I'd like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> Changes ain't totally pleasant but they're excellent things. Two years is about long enough for things to stay exactly the same.  <sub>[v2 c30 P1](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0001)</sub>
